title: Lisse sheaves on a stratum are closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions
statement:
Let $S$ be a topologically Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$.

1. If $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ is an exact sequence of $\Lambda_S$-modules with $F'$, $F''$
   lisse, then $F$ is lisse.
2. If $\phi\colon F\to G$ is a morphism of lisse $\Lambda_S$-modules, then $\ker\phi$ and
   $\coker\phi$ are lisse.

Consequently, for a Noetherian scheme $X$, $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under kernels,
cokernels and extensions in $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, is an abelian category, and
the inclusion is exact. A $\Lambda_X$-module is constructible iff it is lisse on each stratum
of a finite stratification (the scalar ring $\Lambda(*)$ is a field, so a finite constant
local model is a finite free module, [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]).

external.place: (2) The coefficient sheaves $E_S$, $\Qlb_S$ agree with those of Bhatt–Scholze (Lemma 6.8.2 of *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, together with [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]), and their lisse sheaves agree with ours.

(2) The coefficient sheaves $E_S$, $\Qlb_S$ agree with those of Bhatt–Scholze (Lemma 6.8.2 of *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, together with [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]), and their lisse sheaves agree with ours.

proof.text: Compare the two coefficient pullback conventions by Mod.extendScalarsIsoComapInv. A lisse module is locally finitely presented because a finite free module is the cokernel of a zero map. Conversely finite_lf and algcl_lf in CondensedConstructibleSerre apply the existing finite-field and bounded-image algebraic-closure local-triviality theorems. Transport their free local models back along the coefficient isomorphism. This proves lisse iff locally finitely presented on every topologically Noetherian scheme. A finite free local model is a finite constant local model: pull a finite free condensed module back from the point and use preservation of finite biproducts. Rank zero is included.

proof.text: Apply the existing generic lfp_serre_of_locally_free helper from CondensedConstructibleSerre to the local-freeness criterion and freeEpiLocalSplitting. Its proof presents the cokernel, then the image and kernel using local splittings of epimorphisms onto free modules, and splits extensions after locally lifting the quotient basis. Transfer the three assertions through lisse iff locally finitely presented. Isomorphism invariance transfers canonical kernels and cokernels to arbitrary limiting cones and colimiting cocones, giving the ObjectProperty closure classes.

proof.text: On a Noetherian scheme the qcqs branch of IsConstantModelConstructible applies. Prove that its finite constant stratified models are equivalent to IsConstructibleModuleObject. In the forward direction use HasFiniteConstantLocalModel.isLocallyFinitelyPresented and transport the stratum coefficient isomorphism. In the reverse direction each stratum has Noetherian underlying space because its immersion is an embedding; apply the lisse criterion and the finite-free constant model construction of step 1. No Noetherianity of arbitrary covering schemes is assumed.

The existing generic proof intersects the stratifications of the two objects, uses exact inverse image along the strata and the local closure result of step 2. Transfer its conclusions through step 3 to the constant-model constructibility predicate. Prove isomorphism invariance by mapping the presentation isomorphisms and prove zero constructible using the one-stratum identity stratification and the cokernel of an identity on a rank-zero free module.

proof.text: Extension closure gives closure under binary biproducts; their product isomorphisms and zero give finite product closure. Apply Mathlib ObjectProperty abelian-subcategory construction. Its kernel and cokernel preservation lemmas and the additive-functor finite-limit and finite-colimit criteria make the inclusion exact. Finally forget the constructibility-of-subsets field of Scheme.Stratification to obtain FiniteLocallyClosedStratification. Conversely on a Noetherian space every locally closed subset is constructible, so Scheme.Stratification.ofNoetherianSpace restores that field. The local lisse criterion identifies the two formulations, including empty strata and the empty scheme. The Lean argument is conditional on an abstract coefficient ring and its local-freeness criterion; the original theorem applies this proved conditional result directly, then supplies finite_lf or algcl_lf. This avoids a concrete coefficient alias and its costly definitional comparisons without changing any underlying construction.
